reden: The described issue is a Seaport/match-orders edge case where totalExecutions becomes zero (because transfers with to == from are ignored), causing _executionInvariantChecks to be bypassed, yet the protocol still registers the rental and credits escrow, allowing a later stop to drain the escrow. None of the findings in the audit report cover this mechanism. The closest items touch Create/_executionInvariantChecks (e.g., tip items causing stopRent to revert, or zeroed entries from unavailable orders causing a DoS), but those result in reverts/locks, not in creating zero-execution rentals that later drain escrow. The report does not mention the to==from ‘ignored execution’ path, zero-length executions, or fake rentals that credit escrow without transfers. Fixes for the reported issues would not fix the zero-execution escrow drain, so this vulnerability was not detected.
